text: Revolution is the third studio album by American country music singer Miranda Lambert, released on September 29, 2009, via Columbia Records Nashville. The album features the singles "Dead Flowers", "White Liar", "The House That Built Me", "Only Prettier", and "Heart Like Mine", all of which charted on the U.S. Billboard Hot Country Songs chart. Revolution won the Album of the Year award at both the Academy of Country Music Awards in 2010 and the Country Music Association Awards in 2010. Lambert began working on the album in February 2009 and wrote or co-wrote all but four of its 15 tracks. Co-writes were made with her ex-husband and then boyfriend Blake Shelton, who also provides background vocals on "Maintain the Pain", and former Columbia Records artist Ashley Monroe. Charles Kelley and Dave Haywood of Lady Antebellum co-wrote "Love Song", on which they also sing background vocals. The album includes covers of Fred Eaglesmith's "Time to Get a Gun" and John Prine's "That's the Way the World Goes 'Round". To promote the album, an EP titled Dead Flowers was released on September 8, 2009. The lead single, "Dead Flowers", was released in May 2009 after Lambert performed on the 44th Annual Academy of Country Music Awards; it peaked at number 37 on the U.S. Billboard Hot Country Songs chart in July 2009 after spending sixteen weeks on the chart. "White Liar" was released as the second single in August 2009; after Lambert performed it on the 2009 CMA Awards in November 2009, it became her first Top 40 hit on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100, rising from number 66 to number 38, and reached a peak of number 2 on the U.S. country chart in February 2010. "The House That Built Me", the third single, was released in March 2010 and became Lambert's fastest-rising single to date, reaching number 1 on the U.S. Billboard Hot Country Songs chart for the week of June 12, 2010, and staying at number 1 for four consecutive weeks. "Only Prettier" was released as the fourth single on July 26, 2010, debuting at number 45 for the week of July 17, 2010, and peaking at number 12 in December 2010. The fifth and final single, "Heart Like Mine", was released on January 10, 2011. On September 24, 2009, five days before the album's release, Lambert performed all tracks from Revolution in sequence at the Ryman Auditorium. To promote the album, she made appearances on Good Morning America, Late Show with David Letterman, and The Ellen DeGeneres Show during the first week of release, and was featured on the cover story of Country Weekly, as well as in Rolling Stone and US Weekly. Lambert launched her first headlining tour, the Roadside Bars & Pink Guitars tour, which began in March 2010 and included at least 22 stops, such as a performance at the Bonnaroo Music Festival. Upon release, Revolution received universal acclaim from music critics; at Metacritic, it received an average score of 85 based on 11 reviews, indicating "universal acclaim". Rolling Stone praised Lambert as country's most refreshing act, noting her ability to make firearms seem like a matter-of-fact female accessory. Entertainment Weekly described the album as a portrait of an artist in full possession of her powers and called it the best mainstream-country album of the year. The Boston Globe stated that Revolution is the sound of Miranda Lambert coming into her own, and Slant Magazine called it a expansion of her fully realized artistic persona. "The House That Built Me" was ranked number 1 on Engine 145's Best Country Songs of 2009, with "White Liar" at number 11 and "Only Prettier" at number 37. Revolution debuted at number 1 on the U.S. Billboard Top Country Albums chart, marking Lambert's third consecutive Number One album on the chart, and also debuted at number 8 on the U.S. Billboard 200. The album sold approximately 66,000 copies in its first week, her highest first-week total to date. It was certified Gold in February 2010 and Platinum in October 2010 by the RIAA, with total U.S. sales of 1,790,000 copies as of 2016. All information is adapted from the album's liner notes.
